title: Diagnosis document
description: Structured conclusion of a diagnose_issue investigation. Flat operation spec: target file, optional target symbol, change spec, kind, confidence. Feeds the file_ops dispatcher which infers operation (create / patch / add / rewrite) from file existence plus AST parseability.

target_file.description: The file the change targets. May be a path that doesn't exist yet — when it doesn't, file_ops dispatches the create flow automatically.

target_symbol.description: The function / method / class to modify or add. Optional: omit for whole-file operations (create_file, data files). Use the qualified name for methods (e.g. 'StudyEngine._handle_review').

related_symbols.description: Other symbols that must change alongside target_symbol to keep the contract consistent. File-qualified ('path/to/file.py:ClassName.method', preferred) or bare ('ClassName.method', resolved in target_file). At most 6.

root_cause.description: Why the test failed — a bug, missing feature, or behavior gap. Grounded in evidence gathered during the investigation.

change_spec.description: What needs to be true after the change. Concrete enough that the next step can author the fix directly — the patch / add_symbol / create flows read this as their directive.

kind.description: fix: existing code is broken. enhancement: an existing file needs a new symbol or behavior. new_file: a file needs to exist that currently doesn't (file_ops will route to create regardless, but the explicit signal aids diagnosis quality). import_fix: the code is right but a module-level import is missing or wrong in target_file — requires import_statement.

import_statement.description: Required when kind is import_fix: the exact literal import statement to insert, exactly as it should appear in the file (e.g. 'from commands import InventoryCommand'). One complete statement. file_ops routes to the module-frame editor on this — no heuristic extraction from prose.

confidence.description: How confident you are in this diagnosis given the evidence you examined.

recommended_flow.description: Which flow family should apply the change. file_ops: a code or data file change (covers create, patch, add, rewrite internally). project_ops: environment/dependency fix — install a missing package, set up build tools, fix Python path.

secondary_issues.description: Additional issues noticed during investigation; does not block the primary change.

x-example.root_cause: The parser splits on whitespace before stripping quoted segments, so commands with apostrophes fragment.
x-example.change_spec: Tokenize the input with shlex.split before splitting on whitespace.
